questions.q: Match each logic gate to when its output is 1.
pairs: When at least one input is 1
questions.feedback: AND needs both, OR needs one, NOT reverses.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.4 Lesson 1 — Logic gate lab, station 1: The AND gate

questions.q: A two-input AND gate has inputs A = 1 and B = 0. What is its output?
options: It depends on the previous input
questions.feedback: AND gives 1 only when both inputs are 1.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.4 Lesson 1 — Logic gate lab, station 1: The AND gate

questions.q: A two-input OR gate has inputs A = 0 and B = 1. What is its output?
questions.feedback: OR gives 1 when at least one input is 1.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.4 Lesson 1 — Logic gate lab, station 1: The AND gate

questions.q: Complete the truth table for Q = A AND B.
questions.feedback: Only the last row has both inputs at 1, so only the last row gives 1.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.4 Lesson 1 — Logic gate lab, station 1: The AND gate

questions.q: Complete the truth table for Q = A OR B.
questions.feedback: Everything except both-zero gives 1.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.4 Lesson 1 — Logic gate lab, station 1: The AND gate

questions.q: Complete the truth table for Q = NOT A.
questions.feedback: NOT reverses its input: 0 becomes 1 and 1 becomes 0.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.4 Lesson 1 — Logic gate lab, station 1: The AND gate

questions.q: State what the NOT gate does to its input.

markPoints.concept: it reverses it, so 0 becomes 1 and 1 becomes 0

questions.example: It reverses the input, so a 0 becomes a 1 and a 1 becomes a 0.
questions.feedback: Reverses, inverts or gives the opposite — all the same answer.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.4 Lesson 1 — Logic gate lab, station 1: The AND gate

questions.q: Complete the truth table for Q = NOT A AND B.
questions.feedback: NOT A is worked out first, then ANDed with B, so only A = 0 and B = 1 gives 1.
questions.hint: Work out NOT A before the AND.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.4 Lesson 1 — Logic gate lab, station 5: Two-level circuits

questions.q: Complete the truth table for Q = NOT (A OR B).
questions.feedback: The brackets come first: A OR B, then reverse the whole thing. Only both-zero gives 1.
questions.hint: Brackets first, then the NOT across the whole result.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.4 Lesson 1 — Logic gate lab, station 5: Two-level circuits

questions.q: Complete the truth table for Q = A AND (B OR C).
questions.feedback: Three inputs give eight rows. Work out the bracket first, then the AND.
questions.hint: Eight rows, and the first two are done for you.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.4 Lesson 1 — Logic gate lab, station 5: Two-level circuits

questions.q: Complete the truth table for Q = (A AND B) OR (NOT C).
questions.feedback: Two brackets, worked out separately, then ORed together. The output is 1 whenever C is 0, or whenever A and B are both 1.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.4 Lesson 1 — Logic gate lab, station 5: Two-level circuits

questions.q: Why does Q = NOT A AND B give a different answer from Q = NOT (A AND B)?
options: In the first, only A is reversed; in the second, the whole result is reversed
They are the same; the brackets make no difference
The second one cannot be worked out without a third input
The first one reverses B rather than A
questions.feedback: Brackets decide what the NOT applies to, and that changes every row of the table.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.4 Lesson 1 — Logic gate lab, station 5: Two-level circuits

questions.q: A two-input AND gate has inputs A = 1 and B = 1. What is its output?
questions.feedback: AND gives 1 only when every input is 1. This is that case.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.4 Lesson 1 — Logic gate lab, station 1: The AND gate

questions.q: A two-input OR gate has inputs A = 0 and B = 0. What is its output?
questions.feedback: OR gives 1 when at least one input is 1. Neither is, so the output is 0.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.4 Lesson 1 — Logic gate lab, station 1: The AND gate

questions.q: A NOT gate has input A = 1. What is its output?
options: It depends on the other input
questions.feedback: A NOT gate has one input and gives the opposite of it.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.4 Lesson 1 — Logic gate lab, station 1: The AND gate

questions.q: Which of these statements about logic gates are true? Tick all that apply.
options: An AND gate outputs 1 only when all of its inputs are 1
An OR gate outputs 1 when at least one input is 1
A NOT gate has exactly one input
An OR gate outputs 0 only when all of its inputs are 0
An AND gate outputs 1 when at least one input is 1
A NOT gate has two inputs
correct: An AND gate outputs 1 only when all of its inputs are 1
An OR gate outputs 1 when at least one input is 1
A NOT gate has exactly one input
An OR gate outputs 0 only when all of its inputs are 0
questions.feedback: AND wants everything, OR wants anything, NOT takes one input and turns it round.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.4 Lesson 1 — Logic gate lab, station 1: The AND gate

questions.q: State when an AND gate outputs 1.

markPoints.concept: only when every one of its inputs is 1
markPoints.exemplar: Only when all of its inputs are 1.

questions.example: Only when every one of its inputs is 1. If any input is 0 the output is 0.
questions.paraphrase: Just in the case where each input is 1; a single 0 anywhere makes the output 0.
questions.feedback: All of them. An answer that says 'when the inputs are 1' without the 'all' has not said what makes AND different.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.4 Lesson 1 — Logic gate lab, station 1: The AND gate

questions.q: State when an OR gate outputs 1.

markPoints.concept: when at least one of its inputs is 1
accept: at least one|one or more|either|any|any of|a single|one of them|one input|not all|does not need all
markPoints.exemplar: When at least one of its inputs is 1.

questions.example: When at least one of its inputs is 1. It only outputs 0 when every input is 0.
questions.paraphrase: As soon as any single input is 1; the output is 0 only if they are all 0.
questions.feedback: At least one. 'When the inputs are 1' would describe AND, not OR.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.4 Lesson 1 — Logic gate lab, station 1: The AND gate

questions.q: Match each way of writing the same logic to what it means.
pairs: Both A and B have to be true
At least one of A and B has to be true
A and B must not both be true
questions.feedback: The brackets in the last one change everything: it is the AND that is negated, not A.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.4 Lesson 1 — Logic gate lab, station 4: Symbols and pseudocode

questions.q: In a circuit diagram, a gate drawn as a D-shape with a flat back is which gate?
questions.feedback: AND is the flat-backed D. OR has a curved back and a pointed nose, and NOT is a triangle with a small circle.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.4 Lesson 1 — Logic gate lab, station 4: Symbols and pseudocode

questions.q: A gate drawn as a triangle with a small circle on its output is which gate?
questions.feedback: The small circle is what means 'inverted'. The triangle on its own would just pass the signal through.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.4 Lesson 1 — Logic gate lab, station 4: Symbols and pseudocode

questions.q: The output of an AND gate taking A and B is fed into a NOT gate. What expression does the circuit produce?
options: Q = NOT A AND NOT B
questions.feedback: The AND happens first and the NOT is applied to its result, which is exactly what the brackets say.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.4 Lesson 1 — Logic gate lab, station 5: Two-level circuits

questions.q: A and B each go through their own NOT gate, and both results go into an AND gate. What expression does the circuit produce?
options: Q = NOT A AND NOT B
questions.feedback: Each input is inverted before the AND, so each one needs its own NOT in the expression.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.4 Lesson 1 — Logic gate lab, station 5: Two-level circuits

questions.q: Put these stages in the order a circuit for Q = NOT (A OR B) carries them out.
steps: A and B arrive as inputs
The OR gate combines A and B
The NOT gate inverts the result of the OR
Q leaves the circuit as the output
questions.feedback: Working from the inputs towards the output is how a diagram is read, and the order the brackets describe.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.4 Lesson 1 — Logic gate lab, station 5: Two-level circuits

questions.q: Explain why Q = NOT (A AND B) and Q = NOT A AND NOT B are not the same circuit.

markPoints.concept: in the first, the AND is worked out and then inverted
accept: worked out|worked out first|combined|combination|result|invert the result|inverted afterwards|negated afterwards|inverted after|negated after|inverts the output
markPoints.exemplar: In the first, the AND is worked out and then the result is inverted.

markPoints.concept: in the second each input is inverted before the AND
accept: second|other|two not gates|each input|both inputs|separately|own not gate|inverted first|negated first|each one|before they are combined|before combining
markPoints.exemplar: In the second, each input is inverted before the AND sees it.

questions.example: In NOT (A AND B) the brackets are done first: A and B are combined by the AND, and the result is inverted, so the output is 0 only when both are 1. In NOT A AND NOT B each input is inverted on its own first, so the output is 1 only when both are 0. The two circuits agree on two of the four rows and disagree on the other two.
questions.paraphrase: The brackets in the first mean the combination is formed and then reversed, whereas in the second both inputs are reversed individually before being combined.
questions.feedback: Which operation happens first in each. That is the whole difference.
questions.hint: Try A = 1, B = 0 in both and compare.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.4 Lesson 1 — Logic gate lab, station 6: NOT and brackets

questions.q: In the expression Q = NOT A AND B, the NOT applies only to A.
questions.feedback: Without brackets the NOT takes only the thing immediately after it. Brackets are the only way to make it apply to more.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.4 Lesson 1 — Logic gate lab, station 6: NOT and brackets
